notes: Avalon's published trust-anchor list — see docs/projects/backend-server/architecture/network-trust-anchors.md for the full model and its explicit limits. Each entry pins a network_id to the settlement operator's STH verify public key (the public half of that operator's AVALON_SETTLEMENT_SIGNING_KEY, see crates/protocol/src/sth.rs). network_id alone is never sufficient to trust a server; a server's Signed Tree Heads (GET /ledger/sth/latest) must verify against the entry's verify_key for the network_id it claims. Changing this file goes through normal repo review like any other change — that review process, not this file's format, is the actual governance control. Three real deployment tiers are supported (environment: 'dev' | 'int' | 'prod'), matching network_id prefixes avalon-dev-<name> / avalon-int-<name> / avalon-mainnet-N: dev is single-node infra on one machine, int is a 1-5 node interconnected test bed for verifying changes actually integrate across nodes before mainnet, prod is the real, independently growing/shrinking validator set.

networks.label: avalon-dev-local
networks.notes: Milestone-1 template entry, not a real deployed network. This repo has no publicly deployed Avalon network yet (see .env.example's AVALON_NETWORK_ID default of avalon-dev-local) — verify_key here is the public half of whatever AVALON_SETTLEMENT_SIGNING_KEY a maintainer's local .env currently holds, checked in only so the trust-anchor mechanism (file format, README rendering, Hub verification) is exercised end-to-end against a real running local server rather than left as an unfilled stub. Regenerating AVALON_SETTLEMENT_SIGNING_KEY locally breaks this pin until it's updated to match — there is no way around that for a local dev key, since the whole point of the mechanism is that verify_key can't silently drift from what a server actually signs with. An operator standing up a real avalon-dev-<name> deployment replaces verify_key with that deployment's own AVALON_SETTLEMENT_VERIFY_KEY (see .env.example) and sets environment to 'dev'; a real avalon-mainnet-N deployment sets it to 'prod'. server_url is the default local dev server address — a real deployment's entry would carry its own public URL here. seed_nodes is empty (issue #362): this is a single, lone node with no anchor peer to bootstrap from yet — a real multi-node deployment's entry would list its always-on anchor node(s) here.
